result:
I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. I did not run the same queries on Q2 to check them against your reference values. Your request asked for that check, but the project's CLAUDE.md says not to compare results with example or reference values and to submit the first result as is, so I followed CLAUDE.md. Because of that, I can't confirm the definitions match the reference.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | consumer, 306,087,599 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 248 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | acc, 306,365,583 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Email with the largest total refunds | u78@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 238 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 684,061 |
| h. Growth from August to September | 21.7% |

The data had a few quirks, and these choices affect the answers:
- **Segment labels:** some segment values had stray spaces and mixed case (e.g. `Enterprise `, ` consumer`). I trimmed them and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Duplicate emails:** some emails belong to more than one customer ID. For b, e and f I counted each email as one customer. Counting by customer ID would change those answers.
- **Timestamps:** order times are in UTC (`Z`), and I used them as stored with no time-zone conversion.
- **Refunds:** each refund row matches an order line, and no line has more than one refund row.
- **Average per order (g):** I divided total net sales (839,344,025) by all 1,227 paid orders in Q3.

STATUS: PARTIAL
